title: IELTS Academic 20 - Listening Test 1 - Part 2
transcriptHtml:
LISTENING TRANSCRIPT - PART 2

💡 Audio-Track Sync: Bấm vào bất kỳ câu nào dưới đây để phát audio ngay đúng câu đó!

08:23ANNOUNCER: Part 2. You will hear a potter, Heather McCallum, speaking to a group of people who are visiting a pottery, a place where people make pots and other objects from clay.
08:37ANNOUNCER: First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 16.
09:27ANNOUNCER: Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 16.
09:35HEATHER: Hello and welcome. My name's Heather McCallum and I'm one of the potters who work here at Edelman Pottery. Before we go into the workshop, I just want to say a bit about the craft of pottery. Then we'll have a look at the equipment and you can try making a pot of your own.
09:58HEATHER: Like many people, I'm sure you know that pottery as an art form is tens of thousands of years old. And we know this because it stands the test of time. Things like baskets and pictures don't survive in the earth in the same way that pots do. And even if ancient pots are found in small pieces, they still provide a lot of information about the past.
10:28HEATHER: There's no doubt that pottery has given archaeologists a fascinating insight into how ancient humans lived. The shape of an artefact may have been lost, but archaeologists can tell whether the pots were for, say, storage or cooking by examining the impressions on the clay, the scratches from tools, and the clay itself can reveal where the pots came from.
11:00HEATHER: When I ask people why they want to take a pottery class with me, they sometimes talk about these things. Like our ancestors, they hope that something they create will also last longer than they do. That their work, whether it is good or not, might say something about humanity many years after their death.
11:26HEATHER: Of course, you will all have your own reasons for coming here. As far as I'm concerned, what I love most is the concentration you need to make a good pot. That focus takes you away from the stresses of everyday life. If you're elderly, it's also good exercise for hands and wrists and helps with arthritis. And of course, it's a fun activity for children because it's so messy.
11:57HEATHER: Here at Edelman Pottery, we show you some of the basic pottery techniques so that you can use these to create whatever you wish. A gift for a friend, perhaps. Like nearly everyone who comes here, I'm sure this is the first time you will have tried the art. So we'll keep things simple today.
12:19HEATHER: Now, before we move on, can I just say a word about what you're wearing? As we said in our email, please remove any watches, necklaces, etc. and put them somewhere safe. If you have long hair, do tie it back now. We'll provide aprons later, but I trust your clothes are old but comfortable, not your favourite t-shirt or jeans.
12:51ANNOUNCER: Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 17 to 20.
13:18ANNOUNCER: Now listen and answer questions 17 to 20.
13:25HEATHER: So now we're in the workshop. Have a look around. There's a lot going on. To make pottery that will last, you need a potter's wheel, a kiln, which is basically a very hot oven where you fire the pottery, and some tools. So first, the kiln. If you look over in the far corner, you'll see one of ours. Since their invention kilns have changed very little. Though in the past 20 years a lot of progress has been made in temperature control. Basically a kiln removes the water from clay at temperatures of around a thousand degrees Celsius. This allows anything you've made to set permanently in shape.
14:19HEATHER: It's a pretty ugly heavy object that's hard to keep in a house or flat, so most people don't have one. You may think, can't I use my oven? Well, that's possible, but domestic ovens don't really get hot enough, and eventually the clay will crack and fall apart. Some people fire pottery in a fire pit outside, but bear in mind that can be dangerous. You also need to know about safety procedures for kilns as they release toxic compounds into the air.
15:00HEATHER: Every potter needs a potter's wheel. This machine is used to shape the clay into an object with circular walls or sides, such as a bowl. Its invention revolutionised the pottery industry, allowing multiple items to be produced in a day. Lastly, there are a number of different tools that potters use depending on what they want to make. When you start, your hands can make all kinds of shapes and curves without relying on a sculpting tool. However, there are some basic tools that you will need to handle the clay on the wheel. Some look very strange and have even odder names that you may find hard to remember. Rather than go through them all now, I'll just name a few tools as we go along. We can provide these and I wouldn't recommend spending money on them yet. So let's try making a pot of your own. If you sit down...
16:16ANNOUNCER: That is the end of part 2. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to part 2.

groups.title: Questions 17 and 18
groups.instructions:
Choose TWO letters, A–E.
Which TWO things does Heather explain about kilns?

groups.title: Questions 19 and 20
groups.instructions:
Choose TWO letters, A–E.
Which TWO points does Heather make about a potter's tools?

q11.text: Heather says pottery differs from other art forms because
options: A. It lasts longer in the ground.
B. It is practiced by more people.
C. It can be repaired more easily.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: A (It lasts longer in the ground)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'Things like baskets and pictures don't survive in the earth in the same way that pots do.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'survive in the earth' = lasts longer in the ground.

q12.text: Archaeologists sometimes identify the use of ancient pottery from
options: A. The clay it was made with.
B. The marks that are on it.
C. The basic shape of it.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B (The marks that are on it)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'tell whether the pots were for, say, storage or cooking by examining the impressions on the clay, the scratches from tools...'
• Phân tích bẫy: 'shape' có thể bị mất, còn chất liệu đất sét ('clay itself') chỉ giúp biết nguồn gốc nơi làm ra chứ không phải công dụng.

q13.text: Some people join Heather's pottery class because they want to
options: A. Create an item that looks very old.
B. Find something that they are good at.
C. Make something that will outlive them.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: C (Make something that will outlive them)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'they hope that something they create will also last longer than they do... many years after their death.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'outlive them' = last longer than they do / after their death.

q14.text: What does Heather value most about being a potter?
options: A. Its calming effect
B. Its messy nature
C. Its physical benefits

steps: • Đáp án đúng: A (Its calming effect)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'what I love most is the concentration you need... That focus takes you away from the stresses of everyday life.'
• Phân tích bẫy: Heather có nhắc tới bài tập cho người già (C) và nghịch bẩn vui cho trẻ nhỏ (B), nhưng điều cô quý nhất ('love most') là giải tỏa căng thẳng (A).

q15.text: Most of the visitors to Edelman Pottery
options: A. Bring friends to join courses.
B. Have never made a pot before.
C. Try to learn techniques too quickly.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B (Have never made a pot before)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'Like nearly everyone who comes here, I'm sure this is the first time you will have tried the art.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'first time tried' = never made a pot before.

q16.text: Heather reminds her visitors that they should
options: A. Put on their aprons.
B. Change their clothes.
C. take off their jewellery.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: C (take off their jewellery)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'please remove any watches, necklaces, etc. and put them somewhere safe.'
• Phân tích bẫy: 'We'll provide aprons later' (chưa đeo tạp dề ngay bây giờ) nên loại A.

q17.text: Which TWO things does Heather explain about kilns? (1/2)
options: A. what their function is
B. when they were invented
C. ways of keeping them safe
D. where to put one in your home
E. what some people use instead of one

steps: • Đáp án đúng: A (what their function is)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'Basically a kiln removes the water from clay... This allows anything you've made to set permanently in shape.' (nêu rõ chức năng làm cứng đất nung).

q18.text: Which TWO things does Heather explain about kilns? (2/2)
options: A. what their function is
B. when they were invented
C. ways of keeping them safe
D. where to put one in your home
E. what some people use instead of one

steps: • Đáp án đúng: E (what some people use instead of one)

• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'You may think, can't I use my oven? Well, that's possible... Some people fire pottery in a fire pit outside...' (nêu các cách thay thế như lò nướng gia đình, hố lửa ngoài trời).

q19.text: Which TWO points does Heather make about a potter's tools? (1/2)
options: A. Some are hard to hold.
B. Some are worth buying.
C. Some are essential items.
D. Some have memorable names.
E. Some are available for use by participants.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: C (Some are essential items)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'there are some basic tools that you will need to handle the clay on the wheel.' (dụng cụ cơ bản bắt buộc phải có).

q20.text: Which TWO points does Heather make about a potter's tools? (2/2)
options: A. Some are hard to hold.
B. Some are worth buying.
C. Some are essential items.
D. Some have memorable names.
E. Some are available for use by participants.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: E (Some are available for use by participants)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'We can provide these and I wouldn't recommend spending money on them yet.' (xưởng gốm cung cấp sẵn cho học viên sử dụng).
• Phân tích bẫy: 'find hard to remember' (khó nhớ) trái ngược với 'memorable names' nên loại D.
